newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag hopeful of earnings increase in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Viag hopeful of earnings increase in 1997.

text.p: Jochen Holzer, supervisory board chairman of the German diversified utility group Viag AG, said on Thursday that he was optimistic earnings at the group would increase in 1997.
"From our current perspective we are confident that we will be able to keep moving ahead," said Holzer, who added that the group had seen "very, very good growth" in operating profit.
Viag's net profit in 1996 was over one billion marks but Holzer would not specify if the figure referred to the group or to the parent company.
In 1995 the Viag parent company reported net profits of 1.1 billion marks, while the Viag group reported net profits of 1.32 billion marks.
Holzer said Viag would invest an extra 15 billion marks on top of normal investment allocations for strategic purposes, but did not specify an exact time frame for the increased investments.

Viag management board chairman Georg Obermeier last Friday said 1996 had been Viag's most successful year ever, with record profits. He said Viag would at least offer a stable dividend compared with the 1995 payout.
